objects.taxonomy_description: Asian proboscidean measuring 250-300 cm at shoulder weighing 3000-5000 kg. Body massive with thick wrinkled gray-brown skin and sparse body hair. Head broad with twin-domed skull. Ears relatively small compared to African elephant. Trunk (proboscis) elongated and muscular with single finger-like projection at tip. Tusks present primarily in males, shorter than African species. Body barrel-shaped with arched back. Legs pillar-like with five toenails on forefeet. Tail long with terminal tuft. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, sparse hair, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart.

objects.taxonomy_description: Small to medium-sized macropod marsupial measuring 45-105 cm in body length with tail adding 35-75 cm. Exhibits characteristic kangaroo body plan with disproportionately large muscular hind limbs adapted for saltatorial locomotion, small forelimbs with five digits, and thick muscular tail used for balance. Fur coloration varies by species, displaying grey, brown, red, or black tones, often with distinctive facial markings including pale cheek stripes and dark eye bands. Ears are relatively short and rounded compared to kangaroos. Pouch opens anteriorly. Body exhibits bilateral symmetry with digitigrade hind foot posture. Weight ranges 1-25 kg depending on species. Agile leaping gait with tail providing counterbalance during bipedal hopping.

objects.taxonomy_description: Brass wind instrument with compact conical tubing coiled into oval shape. Length approximately 33 cm. Bell flares to 11-12 cm diameter, facing forward. Three piston valves arranged vertically on top with mother-of-pearl or plastic finger buttons. Mouthpiece is cup-shaped, detachable, inserted into leadpipe. Body surface is lacquered brass (golden-yellow) or silver-plated (bright white-metal). Tubing diameter gradually increases from mouthpiece to bell. Valve casings are cylindrical with visible seam lines. Bell rim is rolled edge. Finger hooks and thumb ring present for grip.
